correctness.rationale: For the two minimum-critical-exponent directives, the published classification gives \(a_1\in\{1,3\}\) and a constant tail of exponent \(2\); the proof of Proposition 34 gives odd convergent parities and \(Q_N=2Q_{N-1}+Q_{N-2}\). Theorem 54 therefore specializes to \(R_v(n+1)=n+3Q_{N+1}+Q_N\). Since \(Q_{N+1}/Q_N	o1+\sqrt2\), writing \(m/Q_N	o x\in[1,1+\sqrt2]\) gives the normalized limit \(1+(4+3\sqrt2)/x\). Every \(x\) in the interval is attained by integer choices \(m\) nearest to \(xQ_N\), proving the full cluster interval and its endpoints. The package replay checks the closed form and normalization for both initializations.

value.rationale: The recurrence quotient is a standard quantitative repetitivity invariant, and the source specifically develops recurrence functions for these Rote sequences. The two languages are not an arbitrary slice: they are exactly the languages attaining the minimum critical exponent among binary rich words. Determining the entire normalized cluster interval quantifies their nonconvergent recurrence behavior more strongly than a single limsup and gives an exact invariant common to the extremal pair.
